title.narrative: SAAMEYNTA-SCALING-UP SOLUTIONS TO DISPLACEMENT IN SOMALIA – PHASE 2

description.narrative: Saameynta Phase 2 builds on proven approaches and lessons from Phase 1 to move from piloting to large-scale delivery of durable solutions for displacement-affected communities in Baidoa and Bosaso, Somalia. Aligned with the National Transformation Plan (2025-2029), National Solutions Pathway Action Plan (2024-2029) and government policies, the project strengthens government leadership and coordination, promotes inclusive land governance, expands access to services, and advances economic empowerment and livelihoods. Climate resilience is central to the programme, embedding risk-informed planning, green infrastructure, and adaptive livelihood opportunities to reduce vulnerability to environmental shocks while enabling sustainable, long-term integration. The Saameynta 2 project, is led by the Ministry of interior, Federalism and Reconciliation Affairs under the direct implementation of its subsidiary institutions as relevant and in collaboration with the Ministry of Public Works Reconstruction and Housing and Ministry of Planning, Investment and Economic Development (MoPIED). Incorporating lessons learned from the Phase 1 final evaluation, the project addresses key barriers that exclude IDPs from achieving durable solutions, including tenure insecurity, limited access to livelihoods, and inadequate services. Evidence from the Durable Solutions Progress (DSP) Survey informs targeting and measurement, while recognizing that both IDPs and host communities face significant vulnerabilities that require inclusive, area-based investments. Through a sequenced approach—starting with secure tenure and Area Development Plans, followed by blended financing, private sector engagement, livelihood support, and service delivery—Saameynta Phase 2 aims to create inclusive, climate-resilient urban neighbourhoods that strengthen social cohesion and serve as scalable models for Somalia’s future.

condition.narrative: Social and environmental sustainability will be enhanced through application of the UNDP Social and Environmental Standards (http://www.undp.org/ses) and related Accountability Mechanism (http://www.undp.org/secu-srm).
